task.reverify_note_2: ORCH independently re-checked your BLOCKER finding on TC-ISS-107-04 before dispatching rework. Read tests/integration/helpers.zig TestHarness.init() (lines 413-496): it calls conn.begin() at line 487 BEFORE returning the harness — so h.conn is ALREADY inside an outer transaction from the moment init() returns. deinit() (lines 500-503) unconditionally calls self.conn.rollback(), with the comment 'Never commits — test isolation is guaranteed.' TC-ISS-107-04 (iss107_tenant_storage_mode_test.zig line 186-187) calls `var h = try helpers.TestHarness.init(allocator); defer h.deinit();` immediately. This means the test's own inner `BEGIN`/`SAVEPOINT before_bogus`/`ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT before_bogus` (lines 201-215) is a SAVEPOINT nested inside the harness's own outer transaction, not the outermost transaction boundary — your original review appears to have read the test's inner BEGIN as the only transaction wrapper and concluded the earlier INSERT (line 193) was auto-committed outside it, but it is actually inside the harness's outer transaction the whole time, which h.deinit() unconditionally rolls back at the end of the test regardless of how the test exits. ORCH additionally confirmed empirically: `docker-compose exec -T db_test psql -U bpm -d bpm_test -c "SELECT slug FROM public.tenant WHERE slug='iss107-t4';"` returns 0 rows, even though this exact test has run multiple times already in this session (as part of test-integration-svc and the full test-integration suite during BACKEND-DEV's iterations 1-4 and your own and TEST-RUNNER's verification runs) — if this were a real permanent leak as originally claimed, that row would still be present. Please re-verify your original BLOCKER claim against this evidence. If you agree the leak does not actually exist, note in your result that CODE-DESIGNER's added defensive cleanup in iss107_tenant_storage_mode_test.zig (from rework 2) is unnecessary-but-harmless defensive redundancy, not a functional requirement, and this should not block PASS. Re-validate the rest of the design (GBL-103 migration, lint extension, the blanket completeness audit CODE-DESIGNER redid covering all ~17 INSERT INTO tenant sites) on its own merits.

result.summary: Re-verification per ORCH's reverify_note_2 confirms the original BLOCKER (ISS-0100-REWORK1-VALIDATION-01, iss107-t4 'permanent leak') was a false positive, caused by misreading TC-ISS-107-04's inner BEGIN/SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK sequence as an independent, separately-committed transaction boundary. Independently re-read tests/integration/helpers.zig TestHarness.init()/deinit() (lines 400-504) and confirmed init() opens a real transaction via conn.begin() at line 487 BEFORE returning the harness, and deinit() (lines 500-503) unconditionally rolls it back. Independently re-read TC-ISS-107-04 (lines 182-231) and traced control flow. Independently confirmed vendor/pg/pg.zig's begin()/rollback() (lines 174-184) issue literal BEGIN/ROLLBACK via simpleQuery() with no client-side nesting/refcounting. Then independently reproduced the exact statement sequence against the live db_test Postgres instance (BEGIN; INSERT; BEGIN; SAVEPOINT; failing stmt; ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT; ROLLBACK;): confirmed empirically that a second BEGIN while already inside a transaction block is a genuine no-op (WARNING: there is already a transaction in progress, not an Error) — it does not start a new/nested transaction. This means the test's own inner BEGIN (line 201) never detaches from the harness's outer transaction; SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT (lines 204/215) operate as a true nested savepoint inside that single outer transaction; and the explicit ROLLBACK at line 230 (or, on any earlier assertion failure, h.deinit()'s rollback via the line-187 defer) unconditionally discards the line-193 iss107-t4 INSERT on every code path. Independently queried the live test DB (SELECT slug FROM tenant WHERE slug='iss107-t4') and confirmed 0 rows, consistent with no leak. Verdict: BLOCKER-01 is withdrawn as a false positive. CODE-DESIGNER's rework-2 defensive `defer`-registered DELETE added to TC-ISS-107-04 (§3.6.4 of the design) is correctly characterized by the design itself as harmless, mechanism-independent defense-in-depth against future fragility (e.g. someone later changing the inner ROLLBACK to a COMMIT) — not a required fix for a real current leak. It does not block PASS and does not need to be reverted. Re-validated the rest of the design on independent merits: migration numbering (GBL-103 correctly next after GBL-102, confirmed via `ls migrations/GBL-1*.sql`), the GBL-102-to-GBL-103 AND-narrowing (pure additive `AND slug NOT LIKE 'tc-%'`, cannot widen the guard's pass condition, re-published-not-edited-in-place per the same schema_migrations filename-tracking rationale as GBL-102 itself), the tools/lint_test_isolation.py T060 extension design (independently confirmed against the live script's actual structure: T010-T050 codes, find_test_blocks(), Report/Issue dataclasses, lint_file()/main() all match the design's description; T060 plugs into the same pattern with no conflicting changes), and the build.zig test-integration-env deferral (correctly punted to a separate GitHub issue, not attempted inline). One new MINOR finding from independent re-audit below (documentation-completeness gap in the design's own §3.5 audit narrative, not a functional leak — does not block PASS).

issues.description: WITHDRAWN — false positive. Original claim: tests/integration/iss107_tenant_storage_mode_test.zig TC-ISS-107-04's iss107-t4 INSERT (line 193) is a permanent, uncleaned leak because the slug is not tc-prefixed and no DELETE/defer exists in the test. Re-verification (this pass): TestHarness.init() (helpers.zig line 487) opens a real outer transaction via conn.begin() before returning the harness to the test; TC-ISS-107-04's own inner `BEGIN` (line 201) is issued while already inside that transaction, and PostgreSQL treats a redundant BEGIN as a no-op WARNING (empirically confirmed against the live db_test instance), not a new transaction — so the SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT at lines 204/215 nest inside the single outer transaction, and the explicit ROLLBACK at line 230 (or deinit()'s unconditional rollback via the line-187 defer, on any earlier early return) discards the line-193 INSERT on every path. Empirically confirmed 0 rows for slug='iss107-t4' in the live test DB. No real leak exists. CODE-DESIGNER's added defer-DELETE in TC-ISS-107-04 (rework-2, §3.6.4) is accepted as harmless defensive redundancy, not a functional requirement.

RESOLVED in this design revision — CODE-DESIGNER's §3.5 blanket INSERT-INTO-tenant re-audit (17 files) is a genuine improvement over the original incremental check. No further action required for PASS.

Design §3.5.1's blanket audit file list (17 files) is itself incomplete as a piece of documentation, though the underlying runtime behavior it needed to verify is safe. Independent re-grep of `INSERT INTO (public\.)?tenant` across tests/integration/*.zig surfaces env01_test.zig, env02_test.zig, env03_test.zig, and env05_test.zig as additional sites not on the design's list (distinct from env01_tenant_type_field_test.zig, which the design does list) — each defines its own insertProductionTenant()/insertTestTenant() helpers with tenant_type explicitly passed (not omitted, so out of scope for the omitted-tenant_type audit criterion the design used), and every call site checked (env01 lines 291/294, 375/376, 495/498, 632/635; env02 lines 175/180-181, 234-237/239-240, 308-311/313-314; env03 and env05 analogous) is paired with a `defer cleanupTenantById(...)` registered before the insert. No leak found — this is a documentation-completeness note about the design's own audit narrative undercounting files, not a functional defect, and does not block PASS. Recommend CODE-DESIGNER note this for the audit trail if a future rework revisits this area.
